subject: Different results between lavaan and Mplus when imposing error structure

messages.author: 8ef7c3c36c4d0f37
messages.subject: Different results between lavaan and Mplus when imposing error structure
parts:
I'm imposing an autoregressive error structure on some data in lavaan and Mplus. Syntax for this model appears similar across both software; however, I get different output between the two platforms. Why might this be happening?

I've attached the following files to help:
  • ar_example.png: example of autoregressive error structure from Singer & Willet (2003)
  • ar_lavaan.R: R script that generates data, saves as plain text file, and runs lavaan on the data
  • ar_mplus.inp: Mplus INP file to be run on data outputted from R

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: Different results between lavaan and Mplus when imposing error structure
parts:
Hi,

There was a small error in your code. You generated data d, but analysed data mood:

d <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 200, mu = rep(3.7, 7), Sigma = Sigma)

fit <- lavaan(mod, data = mood, mimic = "mplus”)

After fixing the lavaan call to use the same d, the results are identical

fit <- lavaan(mod, data = d, mimic = "mplus”)

Maybe you had a previously generated mood dataset and were analysing two different data?

Here is a more elegant way of constructing AR1 pattern

rho^abs(row(Sigma)-col(Sigma))

Mikko

parts:
Thank you for noticing that error and providing that code for making the AR1 pattern. It seems, however, that the results of the two software are still not entirely identical; there are differences in the Z statistic when using the simulated data. 

The differences between software are more apparent with what I assume to be non-simulated data found on Dr. Hoffman's book website. The relevant files are attached here. With the attached data, I see differences in standard errors between the two platforms which leads to differences in the Z statistics.
